question: Tejas gets double the amount in 11 years when invested at compound interest, compounded annually. In how many years will the amount become four times itself?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **T** years, it will become **nk** times in **k × T** years.

Given: The amount becomes **2 times** in **11 years**.

Target: The amount needs to become **4 times**, which is **2²** times.

Here, n = 2, T = 11, and k = 2.

∴ Time taken = 2 × 11 = 22 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Principal = P

Amount after 11 years = 2P

Rate of interest = r% (compounded annually)

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc38e9236ae6f9d2e5519929f1ae90c36fa43813cb7411b90ab2160f1b9ecade.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹¹

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹¹ --- (Equation 1)

Let the time taken to become 4 times be **T** years.

⇒ 4P = P(1 + r/100)T

⇒ 4 = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ 2² = (1 + r/100)T

Substitute the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹¹]² = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ (1 + r/100)²² = (1 + r/100)T

Comparing the exponents:

⇒ T = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exponential Growth in CI

In Compound Interest, the amount grows geometrically. If it doubles in 11 years, it will quadruple (2×2) in 11+11=22 years, and become 8 times (2×2×2) in 11+11+11=33 years.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate doubling time: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate of Interest. This is used for mental calculations in finance.

Effective Annual Rate

When interest is compounded more than once a year, the effective rate is higher. Effective Rate = [1 + r/(100×n)]ⁿ − 1, where n is frequency of compounding.</p
